_note: NB315: exclusionary technical terms that have a settled replacement. Off by default — this is a policy a project adopts, not a defect nabokov gets to assert on someone's behalf. Enable with --terminology.
_source: IETF draft-knodel-terminology (Terminology, Power, and Exclusionary Language in Internet-Drafts and RFCs) for the master/slave and whitelist/blacklist pairs and their recommended replacements; the remainder are terms the same discussion settled across the Linux kernel, Python, Git and the major cloud vendors.
_scope: An entry earns its place by having an AGREED replacement, not by someone having objected to the word. Terms whose alternative is still argued over are left out on purpose — 'crazy', 'insane' and 'blind spot' were drafted here and removed, because a linter proposing a substitution nobody has settled on spends the user's trust for nothing, and those are the entries that get a whole rule switched off. Add them locally if your project has decided.
_master: 'master' alone is deliberately absent. It is a master's degree, a master copy, mastering an API, and a Git branch name that millions of scripts hard-code. Only the slave-paired sense is listed, because only that sense is unambiguous.
